The test image shows a tomato field with entire plants collapsing/wilting while still green — no leaf spots, no necrotic patches, just rapid whole-plant collapse. This points strongly toward a wilt disease (bacterial or soilborne). Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Phytophthora_Blight, Verticillium_Wilt.

Based on my observations across 8+ reference views, I can now make my assessment.

**Test image analysis**: A tomato field trial with white plastic mulch and wooden stakes. Entire plants have collapsed/wilted while still mostly green — no leaf spots, no mold, no obvious necrosis. This is an acute, rapid, whole-plant collapse pattern.

**Key evidence**:
- The test image Bugwood ID is **1568047**; the Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference (Bugwood_4) has ID **1568041** — extremely close, suggesting the same photographer/submission documenting the same disease event
- The collapse-while-green pattern is the hallmark of Ralstonia solanacearum (bacterial wilt)
- Phytophthora_Blight shows dark stem lesions; Verticillium_Wilt shows leaf yellowing; Southern_Blight shows white mycelium — none match the field view
- Bacterial_Wilt references show lab streaming tests and one browning/late-stage field shot — less similar to the acute green collapse in the test image
